title.value: Striving for data-model efficiency: Identifying data externalities on group performance
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus on understanding data externalities in machine learning and their impact on group performance, aligning with the core subject of the paper.
title.quote: Striving for data-model efficiency: Identifying data externalities on group performance

extractions.description: The paper explores the concept of data externalities in machine learning, focusing on instances where adding training data from certain sources can decrease model performance on specific sub-groups. It discusses the importance of data-model efficiency for trustworthy and effective machine learning systems and investigates the conditions under which negative data externalities arise. The study examines real-world datasets to understand the operational dynamics of data externalities and suggests ways to mitigate their effects.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily addresses machine learning efficiency and its effects on group performance through data externalities, without a clear connection to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Building trustworthy, effective, and responsible machine learning systems hinges on understanding how differences in training data and modeling decisions interact to impact predictive performance.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus on any specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development theme or application. It centers around improving machine learning model performance and understanding data-model interactions.
primary_category.quote: We seek to better understand how we might characterize, detect, and design for data-model synergies.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper doesn't address secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes. Its focus is strictly on data-model efficiency and externalities in machine learning.
secondary_categories.quote: Our results suggest that data externalities may be surprisingly pervasive in real-world settings, yet avoidable by designing training procedures to promote data-efficiency.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper's focus on data externalities in machine learning does not align with any specified sub-category under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Data externalities directly imply a lower bound on feasible model improvements, yet improving models efficiently requires understanding the underlying data-model tensions.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No secondary sub-categories in Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development are relevant as the paper is primarily concerned with technical aspects of machine learning.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our findings have implications to fairness, privacy, participation, and transparency in machine learning.

applications.justification: The main application discussed is improving data efficiency in machine learning to enhance model trustworthiness and performance across different sub-groups.
applications.quote: We have focused on understanding how and when data externalities manifest across learning settings and training procedures.

new_primary_category.justification: No new category is suggested as the paper lacks relevance to any existing or potential Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development categories.
new_primary_category.quote: Characterizing when and how data externalities can be (i) reliably identified for unknown evaluation groups or large number of groups and (ii) effectively mitigated within reasonable computational limits will be important future work.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category is considered necessary, as the paper's focus on machine learning model efficiency does not translate to an SDD context.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: While this specific type of “data inefficiency” indicates room for model improvement, eq. (4) is likely to be a coarse lower bound for the possible improvements that could be made.
